$comment: Illustrative Safety Perspective fixture. All organizations, records, and results are synthetic. The declarations carry evidence for review, not a safety certification or an independently established authorization.

requirements.name: Therapy command integrity
requirements.description: Only authentic therapy commands are accepted in the stated deployment.
requirements.rationale: Command integrity prevents unintended drug delivery in the classified therapy path.

claims.predicate: REPORT-043 does not invalidate the assessed therapy-path safety requirement or baseline verification.
claims.reasoning: Design inspection establishes that the maintenance icon cannot affect command processing. Existing command-integrity verification applies to the unchanged baseline, so repeating it would not test a changed safety path.

attachment.content: INSPECT-043: firmware 3.2.0 maintenance icon reads a diagnostic-only value. There is no write or control-flow path to therapy command processing. The affected baseline and isolation boundary were inspected.
BASELINE-041: firmware 3.2.0 therapy command-integrity verification passed. REPORT-043 changes neither the baseline nor the assumptions of that verification.

REVIEW-043; subject: asset-tls-path; assessment: assessment-customer-report; disposition: no action for the therapy safety requirement. Reason: design inspection confirms isolation, and baseline verification remains applicable. Reviewer: Example product safety manager; process: Example lifecycle policy P-01 revision 1. No new verification is required for this disposition; other product-quality follow-up is outside this safety assessment.

risks.name: Reported indicator failure considered for therapy impact
risks.statement: If the reported status icon were part of the therapy command path, a hidden unsafe state could affect delivery. Analysis checks this possible connection.

impact.description: Incorrect drug delivery to a patient.

inherentRisk.rationale: Example qualitative hazard-analysis method H-01 revision 1: catastrophic denotes potential death or permanent injury from unintended delivery. No event probability or numeric risk score is asserted.

residualRisk.rationale: The reported maintenance icon is outside the therapy command path. Design inspection and the existing command-integrity verification establish that the report does not invalidate SR-041 or its verification in this baseline.

assessments.name: Safety triage of REPORT-043
assessments.scope: Pump firmware 3.2.0, Globex TLS 1.4.2, and the hospital deployment therapy command path. No claim about other products or deployments.
assessments.summary: Completed triage found no additional safety impact. A justified no-action disposition is recorded for this context; no new verification is required under the example process because the report does not invalidate the existing baseline evidence.

externalReferences.comment: Review record supporting a bounded no-action disposition; not a blanket release approval.

assumptions: The maintenance interface remains isolated from the therapy command path in firmware 3.2.0.

damageScenarios.name: Unintended drug delivery
damageScenarios.description: An unauthentic therapy command changes delivery to a patient.

impacts.description: Potential patient harm from unintended drug delivery; the example severity label is interpreted under the fictional manufacturer hazard-analysis process.

annotations.text: REPORT-043: customer reports a missing status icon in the maintenance interface. Review determines whether the report changes the therapy safety context; no change is presumed.
